entries.name: Villager's Journal
sources: Here There Be Monsters - Curse of Cipactli.esp:BOOK CIPHTBMBookArgJournal1
leaves:
4E 201, 20 Sun's Height

We're on our way at long last. Tee-Kahz insists that this place is a paradise, where we will never have to want again. No more the frigid, fruitless waters of the north. Best fishing in all of Tamriel. Lagoon-of-Many-Fishes, it is called. The place of his birth, a village called Shedet. All I know is I'm already sick of this damnable ship. It's going to be a long journey.

4E 201, 1 Last Seed

Home at last! We have found a place in the village; a small reed hut in the traditional Argonian manner. It's quite cozy, considering. By the gods it's hot here. I've only ever lived in Skyrim. The villagers insist I will adjust. "Remember my roots," and all that. They're friendly enough, though not particularly joyful. They seem excited to have new faces here. None seems to remember Tee-Kahz's family. Or, rather, they do seem to remember, but . . . don't want to talk about it. It's strange, really.

4E 201, 8 Last Seed

Tee-Kahz was right! The fishing here is incredible. The lagoon is teaming with fish. They never seem to run out! Even as the autumn moves in (what autumn there is this far south) the fish only seem to be getting thicker. Even the crops seems to be thriving. Swamp leaf like mad and even wheat! Real wheat, from Cyrodil! In the jungle! I must say, this might have been a good idea. It's good to see Tee-Kahz this alive again.

4E 201, 17 Last Seed

The strangest thing happened this morning. Tee-Kahz awoke with a start, a strange look in his eyes. "Dovahkiin." he muttered, like he was in a trance. He told me later it was the Hist, speaking to him. Speaking to us all. I have been too long away to hear it, they say, but the rest have heard it. Something is happening in this world. Something important. The villagers are visibly shaken today. They keep stealing glances at the old Imperial ruin up on the cliff. Even the weather seems dreary. I feel like there's a massive secret that everybody's in on except me. At least the fishing is still good.

4E 201, 25 Last Seed

I asked one of the villagers about the ruins on the cliff and about the wall beside the village. He seemed friendly enough, but as soon as I asked he hissed viciously. "Mustn't talk about it. You don't need to go in that jungle." I'm afraid to question the others. Tee-Kahz says it's some superstition about the ruins; just the way it's always been. He says that jungle is thick and miserable; we wouldn't want to go there anyway. Yet his eyes don't seems convinced.

4E 201, 13 Hearthfire

Our neighbors left today. Just got on a boat and left, without a word to anyone. Another family did the same a week ago. I don't understand, the fishing is better than ever! Tee-Kahz has been having trouble selling it all. We've never seen such bounty. Yet the villagers just seem to get more and more grim.

4E 201, 1 Frostfall

Another family gone. Not a soul saw them leave. Says their hut was still locked from the inside. Where did they go?? The fish are out of control. They're just starting to rot in the barrels, more than we can possibly sell. We've started feeding them to the turtles in the swamps. The villagers call it an omen, say the Sunken God is awakening. They make signs with their hands and glare at the ruin on the cliff. Tee-Kahz is shaken, I can tell. The stink of fish is heavy in the air.

4E 201, 18 Frostfall

The oarsman have stopped buying our fish. They say there's a taint to the meat, that these waters are cursed. Only a few came to trade this week. They've heard rumors of people disappearing. The captain claims he's seen Naga in the jungles. We've got more than enough saved to support ourselves, but it won't last forever. The villagers have begun whispering about the Legion.

4E 201, 2 Sun's Dusk

We awoke today with a symbol painted on the neighbors' door. Written in blood. A creature, a reptile, with a glaring green eye. "The Sign of Cipactli," Tee-Kahz whispered. The neighbors are gone. The same was drawn on other doors. They were gone, too.

4E 201, 12 Sun's Dusk

The stench of decay is everywhere. Dead fish litter the beaches and flood into the swamps, stinking and rotting. All manner of beast comes to feed on the carrion. The villagers don't bother taking the boats out any longer. I swear I've seen lights on the cliffs, in the ruins. Activity beyond the wall. The Kothringi have come picking through the swamps. They stick to the coast and haven't bothered us. Tee-Kahz says they're not the ones to fear. He says the Legion will take us.

4E 201, 19 Sun's Dusk

They came in the night. I don't know who, but they came. Tore a family from their hut, kicking and screaming. They were Argonians. Soldiers. They wore shiny brass armor, Imperial-like but ancient looking. "You will join the Legion, or feed Cipactli," they growled as they hauled away a mother and her three hatchlings. I think they took them through the gate, into the jungle. When they left they painted the dreaded Sign on her door.

4E 201, 1 Evening Star

Tee-Kahz says we must join them. Whoever they are, they own this lagoon. They always have. He didn't believe it before, but he knows the stories. The Legion. The Sload. Cipactli. We don't belong here. We must join them, or Cipactli will consume us. We haven't gone outside in days. I have seen Naga near the huts, eying the village, hissing their savage calls back and force. I insist we contact the Kothringi; maybe they can help us. Tee-Kahz just laughs and laughs. I don't know who else is left in the village.

4E 201, 3 Evening Star

We awoke this morning with the Sign on our door. Tee-Kahz has run off into the jungle. I locked the gate behind him. He's gone mad. I'll take my chances with the Naga.

4 Evening Star

Fish . . .everything reeks. Naga in the village. Screams. Death. Killed hatchwings. Didn't take the meat. Gods, I'm hungry. A storm is rolling closer. Splitting thunder. I can hear the Hist, now. It calls for Him. "Awaken, awaken, awaken, awaken, awaken." They'll find me. Gods, the smell. Fish. Fish everywhere.

entries.name: An-Xileel Horticulturist's Note
leaves: The cutting we took from the Lilmoth Hist seems to have taken root nicely within the highest room atop our bastion. I admit, I did not expect it to flourish so, perhaps it is the ancient, pre-Duskfall Xanmeer ruins that it takes to like a fleshfly to an open wound, It has, seemingly out of nowhere, facilitated the growth of many new species that of flora that I had not thought present in the Kronka-thtith. Blooms, blossoms and ichors I have harvested and set about to experiment. I hope this Hist will continue to aid my research.

entries.name: Adventurer's Torn Note
leaves: There's something at the end of this maze, I can feel it! It's like my Pa always said: "The moment you stop searching is the moment you miss the big one." He may have been talking about how he almost didn't meet my mother but it sure is a quote to guide a life. I'll just rest here a moment before continuing, that gas almost knocked me out!
